Origin of third part

The third part in X:1 is not part of the tune as recorded by Peter Leatham (and yes, the tune appears in a “hornpipe medley” by Peter Leatham, not Peter Wyper, on “Melodeon Greats”).

It is in fact the third part of a tune recorded by John and Julia Clifford on “Humours of Lisheen” with the somewhat improbable title of “Freddy Kimmel’s” (and which sounds more like a barn dance than a hornpipe) . It appears that Frankie Gavin stuck it onto “Johnson’s” for the De Dannan recording.

Johnston’s, X:4

This is a 4 part version of Johnstone’s hornpipe as played by Tom Ferris and earlier by George Ross from Wexford town. I would expect that Paddy Hayes playing it with 4 parts as mentioned above came from the same source (since Paddy was originally from Piercestown just a few miles outside of Wexford). The extra 2 parts have been attributed I believe to Paddy O‘Brien although it may have been George Ross either as George added additional parts to other tunes. I’ve not notated triplets using the (3 ABC as I find that when the music is replayed using midi it didn’t sound like the boys ’snapped’ their triplets.

↳ Posted by John E Roche on October 18th, 2021.

Re: Johnston’s

Scottish recordings:
The renowned Leith melodeon player James Brown (1880-1919) recorded this tune as “Johnson” in 1909 in a set with “The High Level”. Peter Wyper of the Lanarkshire Wyper Brothers recorded it in 1913, while his brother Daniel released it in 1926 with “The Star” hornpipe and “Millicent’s Favourite”. Peter Leatham from Musselburgh (1885-c1920) recorded it in 1920 along with the “Jessie Smith” hornpipe. Will Starr’s recording is from 1945, again with the “High level” and also “Harvest Home”; he recorded it again in 1954 with the “Trumpet Hornpipe” and the “Violetta Hornpipe”.

In addition, Jack Williams, the “North of England Champion” melodeon player recorded it in 1913. In all of the above it is spelled “Johnson”.
